description:
I fine-tuned Laya, a free open-source Jev alternative, on my MacBook in 98 minutes using data from Firecrawl Alexandria, it went from 44% to 69% accuracy and runs 5x faster, fully offline.

Jev is a decision model that answers fixed questions in milliseconds, but it lives in the cloud. Laya is an open-source model with the same API at just 421M parameters, small enough to run and train entirely on a laptop. The catch: stock Laya only scored 44% on my search-result filtering task. So I fine-tuned it using real data from Firecrawl's Developer Index using Alexandria to see how close a tiny model can get to a 27B cloud giant.

In this video I walk through the full fine-tuning pipeline: collecting ~2,980 search results with Firecrawl's Alexandria, using Claude Opus 5.5 as a teacher model to label them (distillation — the big model teaches once, the tiny model does the job forever), then running the fine-tune on my M5 MacBook Pro with no GPU and no API costs. The final model went from 44% to 68.7% accuracy, matches Jev at spotting which results contain an actual fix, and makes each decision in 53 ms vs Jev's 263 ms round trip.

Jev is still smarter overall, but if you need a small, private, offline decision model for one job, like filtering job listings, finding research papers, or sorting product reviews, this is how to build one for free.
